rules.rule: Redact sensitive entities from prompts and retrieved context before any call to the external model.
Scan model responses for sensitive entities before display or onward transmission; redact matches.
Scan tool parameters for sensitive entities; only per-tool exemptions listed below may pass unmasked to the tool.
Treat tool outputs and retrieved documents as untrusted: scan for prompt-injection signals before they enter the model context.
Log prompts and responses at 'redacted' level only; raw content is never written to the decision log, which is hash-chained and tamper-evident.
Retain decision logs and approval records for 365 days (proposed default — confirm against the obligations register).
Send only the fields required for the task to the model; document lawful basis, retention and cross-border transfer in the privacy assessment.

data_handling.detector_limitations: Built-in detectors are deterministic heuristics for structured identifiers (e-mail, card, IBAN, national IDs, phone, IP, API keys). They do not detect names, postal addresses, free-text health details or paraphrased/non-English injections; layer a dedicated DLP/PII service and a trained injection classifier for production.

entry_criteria: Policy reviewed; deployment of observe mode approved by the AI System Owner
Decision log writing to the hash-chained audit log
Shadow mode evaluating as 'enforce'
exit_criteria: At least 1,000 representative requests evaluated
Would-be decision distribution reviewed by the system owner and security
Sampled would-be blocks reviewed; false-positive rate < 5%
Every legitimate tool seen in traffic has an explicit rule (no legitimate default-deny hits)
Limits calibrated from observed peaks

stages.purpose: Still allow, but surface warnings to the application/operators when the would-be decision is not ALLOW.
entry_criteria: Observe exit criteria met
New policy version approved for warn mode
exit_criteria: Warnings triaged by application owners; no unresolved false-positive patterns
Human-approval workflow tested end-to-end (request → approve/reject → single-use execution)
Alert routing confirmed with on-call teams

stages.purpose: Apply REDACT and TRANSFORM to payloads; blocking decisions are still logged but not enforced.
entry_criteria: Warn exit criteria met
New policy version approved for protect mode
exit_criteria: No raw sensitive data in sampled logs, prompts to the vendor, or responses
Task quality impact of redaction reviewed and accepted by the business owner
Adversarial (prompt-injection / leakage) test results reviewed

stages.purpose: Full decisions: DENY, REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL, ESCALATE and RATE_LIMIT block execution.
entry_criteria: Protect exit criteria met
Kill-switch drill passed (contain test below)
New policy version approved for enforce mode by all required approver roles
exit_criteria: Steady state: false-positive rate and approval latency within agreed targets
Monitoring alerts and review cadence operating
Periodic policy review scheduled

stages.purpose: Incident state, not a promotion target: kill switch active for the whole policy scope; every in-scope request is denied. Rehearse it before enforcement and use it during incidents.
entry_criteria: Drill: scheduled test window approved
Incident: authorized role engages the kill switch
exit_criteria: Drill: measured time-to-disable ≤ 15 minutes and full DENY confirmed in the decision log

rules.rule: Redact sensitive entities from prompts and retrieved context before any call to the external model (Azure OpenAI).
Scan model responses for sensitive entities before display or onward transmission; redact matches.
Scan tool parameters for sensitive entities; only per-tool exemptions listed below may pass unmasked to the tool.
Treat tool outputs and retrieved documents as untrusted: scan for prompt-injection signals before they enter the model context.
Log prompts and responses at 'metadata' level only; raw content is never written to the decision log, which is hash-chained and tamper-evident.
Retain decision logs and approval records for 730 days (proposed default — confirm against the obligations register).
Send only the fields required for the task to the model; document lawful basis, retention and cross-border transfer in the privacy assessment.
Confirm Azure OpenAI contract terms on data use, retention, training opt-out and incident notice before production traffic.
Outbound sends and exports carry only data required by the bound case; bulk egress requires approval and row caps.
